effects: Only the registry owner can call it (onlyOwner). It requires the token to be registered already and the cross-chain token to be non-zero.
Appends a record {chainId, crossChainToken, isActive: true} to the token's crossChainRecords array. Existing records stay, and no tokens or ETH move (not payable).
formats.shown: "Add cross-chain record" with the Base token, the other chain's ID as a raw number, and the cross-chain token address.

findings.title: addCrossChainRecord shows _chainId as a raw number instead of the chainId format that names the chain.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json: {"path":"_chainId","label":"Chain ID","format":"raw"}. Case 1 screen shows 'Chain ID: 1'. The spec defines a `chainId` format ('Ethereum Mainnet' for 1).
findings.fix: Use "format": "chainId" on _chainId and label it 'Other chain'.

findings.title: addCrossChainRecord resolves the cross-chain token's name on Base, though the token lives on _chainId.
findings.evidence: AssetIdentityRegistry.sol addCrossChainRecord: '@param _crossChainToken Adresse du token sur l'autre chain'. descriptor.json: _crossChainToken addressName with types [token] and no chainIdPath. Case 1 passes mainnet USDC 0xA0b8…eB48 with chainId 1. Resolved on Base, this address is unknown or names another contract.

formats.key: registerAsset(address _tokenAddress, uint8 _assetClass, uint8 _backingType, string _legalIdentifier, string _jurisdiction, string _custodian)
effects: Only the registry owner can call it. It requires a non-zero token that is not registered yet and a non-empty legal identifier.
Creates an active identity record for the token with the given asset class, backing type, legal ID, jurisdiction and custodian, and records the signer as registeredBy.
If the legal identifier is already registered, the asset is flagged isDuplicate and DuplicateDetected is emitted.
Adds the token to the identifier index and the asset list. No tokens or ETH move (not payable).
formats.shown: "Register asset ERC-8240" with the token, asset class and backing (enum names), legal ID, jurisdiction and custodian.

findings.title: registerAsset intent uses the jargon 'ERC-8240', which tells a normal signer nothing.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json registerAsset: "intent": "Register asset ERC-8240". The code registers an identity record (AssetIdentity) in a registry.
findings.fix: Use an intent like 'Register asset identity' and add an interpolatedIntent naming the token and asset class.

findings.title: registerAsset may flag the asset as a duplicate, based on storage the screen cannot show.
findings.evidence: AssetIdentityRegistry.sol registerAsset: 'if (identifierExists[_legalIdentifier]) { isDuplicate = true; ... emit DuplicateDetected(...) }'. The result depends on registry state, not calldata.

findings.title: registerAsset test case 0 uses mainnet DAI's address as the token on Base.
findings.evidence: cases/0.json: chainId 8453, token 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F (DAI on Ethereum mainnet). It renders as a raw address.
findings.fix: Use a token deployed on Base in the test.

effects: Only the registry owner can call it, and the asset must be registered.
Sets the token's identity isActive to false and updates updatedAt. There is no function to re-activate it, and registerAsset rejects tokens already registered, so this is permanent.
Emits AssetRevoked with the reason. No tokens, approvals or ETH move (not payable).
formats.shown: "Revoke asset" with the token and the reason text.

findings.title: revokeAsset intent 'Revoke asset' is vague and does not say the revocation is permanent.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json: "intent": "Revoke asset". AssetIdentityRegistry.sol revokeAsset: 'identities[_tokenAddress].isActive = false;'. No function sets isActive back to true, and registerAsset requires '!isRegistered[_tokenAddress]'.
findings.fix: Use an intent like 'Revoke asset identity (permanent)' and an interpolatedIntent 'Revoke registry identity of {_tokenAddress}'.
